observations: A single solar panel with a white frame and dark cells.
The cells appear to be monocrystalline and use a half-cut design.
A watermark reading 'ZICO SOLAR ENERGY' is visible across the center of the photo.
No manufacturer name, brand, or technical specification label is visible on the front of the panel.
The panel is leaning against a wall in an indoor setting, possibly a warehouse or shop.

claims.evidence: The wattage is not visible on the front; the technical label on the back is missing from the photos.
Photo 0 shows the dark, uniform cell structure typical of monocrystalline solar panels.

risks.risk: Actual wattage may be lower than claimed.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's specification label on the back of the panel.

risks.risk: The panel may be non-functional or have significantly degraded output.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter reading the open-circuit voltage (Voc) and short-circuit current (Isc) in full sunlight.

risks.risk: Internal cell damage (micro-cracks) not visible to the naked eye.
risks.proof: An electroluminescence (EL) test image, or at minimum, high-resolution close-ups of the glass surface.

proof_requests: Photo of the technical specification label on the back of the panel.
Video of a multimeter test showing the panel's output in direct sunlight.
Close-up photos of the front glass to check for chips or cracks.
response.reason: The wattage, which is the primary factor for pricing a solar panel, cannot be verified without a photo of the specification label on the back. The current photo only confirms the type (monocrystalline) but not the capacity.
